name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Budzinski holds a roughly $2.9M-to-$25K cash advantage over Wilson, a massive resource gap
Incumbent Democrat running in a district that leans Democratic by about five points
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
No public general-election polling, so the estimate rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: an incumbent in a D+5 district with a nearly hundred-to-one cash advantage and markets pricing her win around 95 percent. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a sharply favorable national environment for the GOP could narrow the margin enough to matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Democratic incumbent Nikki Budzinski seeks another term in a central Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised more than $3.5 million and holding roughly $2.9 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised about $495,000 with under $30,000 available. Outside spending has been minimal on both sides.

No public general-election polling tracks the race, and national raters have not flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 95 percent. The combination of incumbency, the district's partisan lean, and the fundraising gap leaves Wilson a narrow path to an upset, though the absence of polling adds some uncertainty about the final margin.
